meta.name: Felper
meta.summary: Eleven traced workflows through Forge: inspect the components, follow each execution path, and review its checks and known failure modes.
meta.description: Forge is a Windows Electron desktop application used to prepare product content, images, properties and vehicle fitments, then execute operator-triggered actions in a Back Office system. The renderer manages input and review; the Electron main process owns browser automation, filesystem access and database reads. This implementation reference preserves the supplied component and workflow descriptions, with internal hostnames replaced by system roles.
invariants: Titles must be POSTed one language per request. A batched array only ever persisted EN.
Nearly every write runs inside a the Back Office admin application page, because the session cookie only attaches from that origin.
openBoAndFill (DOM injection) is the only path that persists attributes. The attributes batch tool loops through it deliberately.
Injected scripts are IIFEs returning a Promise; the caller relies on awaitPromise. A non-async wrapper silently serialises to {} and makes every check pass.
setReactValue writes through the native prototype setter. Assigning el.value directly is invisible to React.
sleepNet is never scaled by speedFactor. The speed slider may only compress UI waits, never network floors.

contexts.label: Renderer
contexts.description: The Felper UI. Vanilla DOM in app/index.html + app/app.js. Reaches the main process only through window.felperElectron.

contexts.label: Main process
contexts.description: Node.js side. Owns every BrowserWindow, all Chrome automation, the SQL read layer and the filesystem.

contexts.label: Page context
contexts.description: Code that runs inside someone else's page — the Back Office admin application or the image management application — not in our renderer. Dashed because it is temporarily attached to a document we do not own.

contexts.label: External
contexts.description: Systems outside this codebase: the BO stack, real Chrome, SQL Server, supplier sites.

nodes.label: Inputs tab
nodes.summary: Product entry. Single mode takes a BO code and an AI-generated JSON reply; batch mode takes 2–20 rows or an Excel import, then previews and runs them.

nodes.label: IMG tab
nodes.summary: Photo library plus the multi-source Image Importer: scrape, drag-drop, folder load, one photo to many codes, then upload and verify.

nodes.label: CMS tab
nodes.summary: Generated titles, subtitles, descriptions and article HTML in six languages, plus the batch review navigator.

nodes.label: Properties & CSE tabs
nodes.summary: Physical specs and the five comparison-shopping channels (Skroutz, BestPrice, NexTag, Google, Linkwise), including a CSE batch runner.

nodes.label: Compatibilities tab
nodes.summary: Vehicle-fitment matching against a bundled read-only dictionary of several thousand rows, plus BO dimension display.

nodes.label: BO Bind tab
nodes.summary: The main fill trigger. '⚡ Fill Selected' runs the whole API pipeline; also holds bulk category binding and the section checkboxes.

nodes.label: EDIT tab
nodes.summary: Patching live products, plus six one-off batch tools: dimensions, BLK filler, bind article, clone articles, category FAQ, attributes.

nodes.label: BO Auditor tab
nodes.summary: Read-only catalogue audit. Only check A1 (part-number / title integrity) is live; A2–A7 are disabled placeholders.

nodes.label: History & analytics
nodes.summary: Per-day productivity log, archived days, batch dashboard and CSV export. Timed panels in single mode, batch panels in batch mode.

nodes.label: state object
nodes.summary: DEFAULT_STATE — one object holding mode, product fields, checklist, timers, history and the image library. Everything resets on load except PERSISTENT_FIELDS, so the app always opens blank and the BO code decides the mode.

nodes.label: Image processing
nodes.summary: Canvas plus the vendored pica resampler: square-fit to a 900px content box on a 1000px canvas, flood-fill background to white, crop, and the square-position editor.

nodes.label: collectBoPayload()
nodes.summary: The canonical single-product payload: boCode, properties, cse, cms{titles,subtitles,descriptions}, articles, articleHtml, attributes, speedFactor. Callers add _sections, _isPatch, _isBatch and _expectedTitle.

nodes.label: Templates & helpers
nodes.summary: Per-mode title / description / subtitle templates, translations, CSE and attribute presets, BO category links. Selected by setup mode (oil, air, car, generic, batch).

nodes.label: compat-matcher
nodes.summary: Pure matching engine over a large minified compatibility dictionary — model key normalisation, engine and year extraction. Exposed as window.FelperCompat.

nodes.label: bo-batch-payloads
nodes.summary: Pure builders and guards for Clone Articles and Category FAQ. The only module loaded by all three of the renderer, the main process and the test suite.

nodes.label: localStorage
nodes.summary: Key oilFilterWorkflowHelperState holds the whole state object; a second key holds the last auditor run.

nodes.label: IndexedDB
nodes.summary: Two databases: oilFilterWorkflowHelperImages (browser-path image bytes) and felperBatchDash (saved batch runs). In Electron, images are real files on disk referenced by path.

nodes.label: window.felperElectron
nodes.summary: The only door between renderer and main: contextBridge methods mapping to IPC channels, plus 8 progress-event subscriptions. Loaded solely by the main window.

nodes.label: window.felperBo
nodes.summary: A six-line second bridge injected into every BO window. Exposes only pressTab() and pressEnter(), because PrimeVue's auto-save needs a genuinely trusted key event.

nodes.label: IPC router
nodes.summary: The ipcMain handlers covering fills, photos, scrapers, batch tools, the auditor and file operations, plus 8 channels pushed back to the renderer.

nodes.label: ERP description fetch
nodes.summary: Three-level lookup that also drives automatic mode detection: 10-minute memory cache, then a learned API URL template, then a full page load with a fetch interceptor and a CDP network listener.

nodes.label: fillCmsViaApi
nodes.summary: The current default write path. One large inline script inside the authenticated BO page posts titles, descriptions, dimensions, attributes, properties, CSE binds and articles straight to the APIs — no DOM driving.

nodes.label: openBoAndFill
nodes.summary: The DOM-injection path: opens the product page, runs guards, injects bo-fill.js, then follows the captured article URL into phase 2. Still the only path that persists attributes.

nodes.label: fillBoInChrome
nodes.summary: Same phase-1 script, but executed in the operator's real Chrome over CDP. Kills any running Chrome first, because a live profile lock makes Chrome ignore --remote-debugging-port.

nodes.label: openBoAndVerify
nodes.summary: Read-only inverse of the fill: injects bo-verify.js, reads values back and returns an issue report. The async injection wrapper is load-bearing — a plain wrapper serialised the unresolved Promise and made everything falsely pass.

nodes.label: IMG Tool upload
nodes.summary: Two upload paths: a UI-driving one that opens the product and confirms identity from its store, and an API-fast one that reads the pUID from BO then posts images directly. Fast skips the already-has-photos guard.

nodes.label: Batch operations
nodes.summary: Dimensions, BLK Sprint Boosters, bind article, clone articles, category FAQ and attributes. Each navigates once and loops in-page, streaming progress back per code.

nodes.label: Supplier scrapers
nodes.summary: InterCars and AutoDoc image discovery. Both refuse a loose match: short codes are rejected outright and the slug must contain a delimited, in-order token match — never just the first link.

nodes.label: bo-auditor
nodes.summary: Orchestrates catalogue checks: pulls the product catalogue, derives a brand per product from part-number patterns, runs check A1 and streams progress.

nodes.label: bo-db (read-only)
nodes.summary: The SQL layer, read-only by construction: readOnlyIntent, and assertReadOnly() rejects anything but a single SELECT or WITH, plus stacked statements. Credentials come only from process.env.

nodes.label: cdp-client
nodes.summary: A dependency-free CDP client that hand-rolls the WebSocket protocol over raw sockets. One socket per command. Rewrites localhost to 127.0.0.1 because Windows resolves localhost to ::1 while Chrome listens only on IPv4.

nodes.label: BO request logger
nodes.summary: webRequest observer on the BO session recording every POST, PUT and PATCH with up to 8 KB of body — the forensic trail behind every wrong-product guard in this codebase.

nodes.label: userData files
nodes.summary: %APPDATA%/felper — rolling 7-day state backups, photo and request logs, scrape cache, processed images, Dropbox cache, and original-image backups for revert. Pinned to the felper folder so data survived the rename.

nodes.label: boFetchWindow (hidden)
nodes.summary: A never-shown BrowserWindow on the BO session, used only to scrape ERP description, dimensions and vehicle type. Its CDP network listener must be attached before loadURL or it misses the response.

nodes.label: boWindow
nodes.summary: The visible workhorse. One module-level singleton reused by fourteen call sites, on partition persist:bo-session so the login survives. Broadcasts every navigation back to the renderer.

nodes.label: imgToolWindow
nodes.summary: The IMG Tool automation window on its own session. Driven with real synthesised mouse events, because the autocomplete selects on mousedown and ignores element.click().

nodes.label: Scrape windows
nodes.summary: One window per supplier, each on its own session. Shown with showInactive so they never steal focus but the operator can still solve a Cloudflare challenge.

nodes.label: Real Chrome
nodes.summary: The operator's own Chrome, relaunched against their real User Data directory with --remote-debugging-port=9222 so they are already logged in everywhere.

nodes.label: Inline API scripts
nodes.summary: Template-literal scripts authored in main.js and executed inside the BO page — the CMS pipeline and every batch tool. They run there, not in Node, because the session cookie only attaches from that origin.

nodes.label: bo-shared.js
nodes.summary: Helper prelude textually prepended inside the wrapper. Provides setReactValue, which uses the native prototype setter — assigning el.value directly is invisible to React.

nodes.label: bo-fill.js
nodes.summary: Phase 1: CMS, properties, CSE and attributes by driving the real React UI. Three sleep tiers, where the network tier is never scaled by speedFactor. Ends by capturing the article-edit URL.

nodes.label: bo-article-fill.js
nodes.summary: Phase 2: writes the article body into TinyMCE once per language and saves, up to three attempts each. Saves by invoking the button's React onClick prop, which bypasses the disabled state.

nodes.label: bo-verify.js
nodes.summary: The same traversal as bo-fill, but it clicks, reads and presses Escape instead of writing. Cross-checks identity by reading the Part No. from the BASIC INFO tab.

nodes.label: correlator API
nodes.summary: The main write API: titles, descriptions, attributes, properties, dimensions, CSE binds and category binds. Titles must be posted one language at a time — a batched array only ever persisted EN.

nodes.label: bo-agg API
nodes.summary: Article upsert, keyed by Code (language plus name) and pUID. One POST per article per language.

nodes.label: BO admin site
nodes.summary: The React admin the whole app exists to fill. PrimeReact widgets, TinyMCE article editor, and auth by session cookie — which is why nearly every write runs inside one of its pages.

nodes.label: IMG Tool
nodes.summary: The image pipeline. POST /resize/images twice per image — multipart upload, then a JSON record carrying uid, colour and the eight output sizes.

nodes.label: InterCars · AutoDoc
nodes.summary: Supplier catalogues scraped for product photos. AutoDoc images are upscaled by probing the CDN's size parameter and measuring naturalWidth in-page.

nodes.label: e-dnafilters.gr
nodes.summary: The public DNA storefront, scraped for the Greek 'Χρήση Φίλτρου' (filter use) value with up to three progressively shorter query variants.

nodes.label: SQL Server
nodes.summary: Read from two tables, _erp_Products_Full and _Products_Title, joined in JavaScript rather than SQL to dodge a Greek/Latin1 collation conflict.

nodes.label: Dropbox
nodes.summary: Air supplier photo archives. The share link's browser-session token is stripped and dl=1 forced; the zip is extracted with PowerShell Expand-Archive.

edges.label: product fields
edges.note: The BO-code prefix also drives automatic mode selection.

edges.label: 6-language copy
edges.note: renderGeneratedOutputs() re-renders every grid from the parsed title.

edges.label: reads copy-cards
edges.note: CMS values are read positionally out of the rendered textareas, then mapped to the language order.

edges.label: specs + 5 channels
edges.note: Property rows differ by mode: air and car carry airflow figures, oil carries height and diameter.

edges.label: 8 progress streams
edges.note: Per-code progress pushed back so the renderer can render a live log.

edges.label: require() — same module
edges.note: The one module shared by renderer, main process and tests. Pure by design; the fetching lives in main.js.

edges.label: cdpEvalAsync
edges.note: awaitPromise:true — this is why every injected script returns a Promise.

edges.label: drives React DOM
edges.note: A Tab keydown is what triggers BO's own auto-save API — the script never calls fetch itself.

edges.label: felperBo.pressTab()
edges.note: The page asks the main process for a trusted key event, because a synthetic one does not trigger the auto-save.

edges.label: persist:bo-session
edges.note: The partition is what keeps the operator logged in across runs.

edges.label: alt_image by reference
edges.note: Variations reference existing CDN URLs rather than re-uploading, which would duplicate them into the general pool.

flows.label: Fill BO — API pipeline
flows.summary: The current default write path. Everything goes through the correlator and bo-agg APIs from inside an authenticated page — no DOM driving at all.

steps.label: Operator clicks ⚡ Fill Selected
steps.detail: fillViaApiAction(), also bound to every .fill-via-api-btn across the tabs.

steps.label: Renderer assembles the payload
steps.detail: Waits for any in-flight filter-use fetch first, then repacks into cms, articleHtml, properties, attributes and cse, gated by the section checkboxes.

steps.label: Crosses the context bridge
steps.detail: felperElectron.cmsFillViaApi(boCode, data) — the renderer has no other way to reach Node.

steps.label: BO product page opens
steps.detail: Waits for a GUID-shaped input, which is how it knows the product UID has rendered.

steps.label: Identity guards run before any write
steps.detail: Patch payloads must match the URL and clear a 50% title-word threshold, or the fill aborts rather than overwrite the wrong product.

steps.label: One inline script runs inside the page
steps.detail: It runs there, not in Node, because the session cookie only attaches from the the Back Office admin application origin.

steps.label: Writes hit the correlator API
steps.detail: Descriptions batch, but titles go one language per POST — a batched array only ever persisted EN.

steps.label: Articles upserted per language
steps.detail: Then shared DNA articles, cached per session from a reference product.

steps.label: Log rendered back in the UI
steps.detail: renderFillLog() — optionally followed by a category bind and a photo upload in the same run.

failureModes.symptom: { needsLogin: true } and nothing is written
failureModes.cause: The persist:bo-session cookie expired, so the product URL redirected to the login page.
failureModes.check: Open any BO window and log in once. The session is shared by every window on that partition, so one login fixes all paths.

failureModes.symptom: { mismatch: true } — the fill refuses to run
failureModes.cause: The title-word guard found under 50% of the expected title words on the loaded page. Usually the BO code and the pasted content belong to different products.
failureModes.check: Confirm the bo_code in the JSON matches the product you meant. This guard exists because a live product was once overwritten.

failureModes.symptom: Only EN titles land, other languages silently missing
failureModes.cause: Titles were posted as a batched array instead of one request per language.
failureModes.check: The per-language POST loop must stay a loop. Never 'optimise' it into a single batched call.

failureModes.symptom: Titles or subtitles come back blank on one side
failureModes.cause: Only one of title/subtitle was supplied for a language, and the live re-read of the CMS tab failed, so posting would have blanked the other side.
failureModes.check: The code deliberately skips the POST in this case. Supply both sides, or check that the CMS Setup tab rendered.

failureModes.symptom: Attributes appear unchanged after a successful run
failureModes.cause: The API path does write attributes, but keyword/video edits made only in the UI cards are not in the payload unless the Attributes checkbox is ticked.
failureModes.check: Tick Attributes in the Advanced panel, or use the EDIT tab attributes batch tool, which routes through the DOM path.

flows.label: Fill BO — DOM injection
flows.summary: The older path that drives the real React UI. Still the only route that persists attributes, so the attributes batch tool loops through it deliberately.

steps.label: Batch or retry action fires
steps.detail: Also reached from Retry Last Fill, the CSE batch, the EDIT patch runner and the batch-CMS navigator.

steps.label: Payload gains its section allowlist
steps.detail: _sections decides which of cms, properties, cse, attributes and articleCreate run.

steps.label: Window loads and clears four guards
steps.detail: Title-word match, login redirect, URL identity, then a wait for the React tab list to exist.

steps.label: Prelude prepended
steps.detail: setReactValue writes through the native prototype setter — assigning el.value directly is invisible to React.

steps.label: bo-fill.js injected and awaited
steps.detail: The script is an IIFE returning a Promise; the caller relies on awaitPromise.

steps.label: It drives the real UI
steps.detail: Fills a cell, then sends Tab — BO's own keydown handler is what saves.

steps.label: Trusted keys come back through IPC
steps.detail: A synthetic key event does not satisfy PrimeVue, so the page asks the main process to send a real one.

steps.label: Article URL captured, phase 2 follows
steps.detail: window.open, pushState and replaceState are monkey-patched to capture the URL without spawning a tab, then all three are restored.

failureModes.symptom: Fill finishes instantly with filled: 0
failureModes.cause: The React tab list never appeared within 15s, so no section could be located.
failureModes.check: The BO page is slow or partially rendered. Reload the product page manually and retry.

failureModes.symptom: Some values are typed but not saved
failureModes.cause: The Tab keydown that triggers BO's auto-save did not register as trusted.
failureModes.check: Confirm bo-preload.js is still set as the window's preload — felperBo.pressTab() is what makes the key event real.

failureModes.symptom: Dropdown picks the wrong item
failureModes.cause: The dropdown filter only engages above six items, and the search term is truncated to the first three alphanumerics (K&N becomes K).
failureModes.check: Verify the intended option against the match ladder before assuming the value was wrong in the payload.

failureModes.symptom: Everything is slower or flakier after changing the speed slider
failureModes.cause: speedFactor scales the micro and UI sleeps only. If a network wait was scaled by mistake, requests get cut off.
failureModes.check: sleepNet must stay unscaled. Never multiply it by speedFactor.

failureModes.symptom: A second browser tab opens during the fill
failureModes.cause: The window.open monkey-patch was not restored, or an exception skipped the restore.
failureModes.check: window.open, pushState and replaceState must all be restored on every exit path.

flows.label: Phase 2 — article in 6 languages
flows.summary: Writes the article body into TinyMCE once per language. The trickiest injection in the codebase, and the one with the most defensive machinery.

steps.label: Phase 1 returns an articleEditUrl
steps.detail: Captured from the '+ New Article' button without letting a real tab open.

steps.label: Same window navigates to the editor
steps.detail: Relative URL resolved against the Back Office admin application; login redirects detected explicitly.

steps.label: Waits for TinyMCE to truly initialise
steps.detail: Polls up to 30s for #Name, the editor container and activeEditor.initialized — three conditions, because any one alone lies.

steps.label: bo-article-fill.js injected in an async wrapper
steps.detail: bo-shared is deliberately not prepended here; this script inlines its own setters.

steps.label: Language switched via React onClick
steps.detail: A plain .click() does not update the controlled dropdown state, so the prop is invoked directly.

steps.label: Editor reinitialises, script waits again
steps.detail: BO replaces the TinyMCE instance on every language switch.

steps.label: Content set, then saved past the disabled state
steps.detail: The Save button's React onClick is called directly, which bypasses the disabled attribute entirely.

steps.label: Whole phase races a 120s hard timeout
steps.detail: did-navigate-in-page is deliberately not used as the completion signal — BO fires it on every language switch, which would resolve after one language.

failureModes.symptom: Only the EN article is written, the rest are missing
failureModes.cause: Completion was signalled by a navigation event that BO fires on the first language switch.
failureModes.check: The phase must be bounded by the injected script's own Promise plus the 120s race — never by did-navigate-in-page.

failureModes.symptom: Article body is empty but the save succeeded
failureModes.cause: TinyMCE was replaced after the language switch and setContent hit the stale editor instance.
failureModes.check: The 15s reinit poll must complete before writing. Confirm activeEditor.initialized is true.

failureModes.symptom: Save button stays greyed out and nothing persists
failureModes.cause: The button is React-controlled; removing the disabled attribute alone does not fire the handler.
failureModes.check: Save via the __reactProps onClick path. The DOM-click fallback is only a last resort.

failureModes.symptom: Phase 2 never starts
failureModes.cause: Phase 1 did not capture an articleEditUrl, so there was nothing to navigate to.
failureModes.check: The '+ New Article' button must exist on the CMS tab, and the articleCreate section must be enabled in _sections.

flows.label: ERP description lookup
flows.summary: Three escalating levels behind a single call. Level 3 teaches the app the API URL template, which promotes every later code to level 2 — roughly 200ms instead of a full page load.

steps.label: Operator types a BO code
steps.detail: Debounced 400ms; the prefix alone already picks oil or generic mode.

steps.label: Level 1 — 10-minute memory cache
steps.detail: Returns instantly with no window and no network.

steps.label: Level 2 — learned API template
steps.detail: One fetch inside the already-authenticated hidden window. On a miss the template is invalidated and it falls through.

steps.label: Level 3 — CDP listener attached first
steps.detail: It must be attached before loadURL, or the dimensions response has already gone by.

steps.label: Page loads with window.fetch monkey-patched
steps.detail: Every response is cloned and searched for a key matching /^erp.?desc/i; a DOM TreeWalker is the fallback.

steps.label: The API URL is turned into a template
steps.detail: The code is replaced with a placeholder — this single line is what makes every subsequent lookup fast.

steps.label: Result drives automatic mode selection
steps.detail: detectModeFromErpDesc picks oil, air or car; a vehicleType of car upgrades air to car; unclassifiable falls back to generic.

failureModes.symptom: 'ERP Description not found — make sure you are logged in to BO'
failureModes.cause: Neither the fetch interceptor nor the DOM fallback found a description within 15s.
failureModes.check: Log in to BO once in any window. If already logged in, the product may genuinely have no ERP description.

failureModes.symptom: Dimensions are missing but the description arrives
failureModes.cause: The dimensions race timed out at 5s, so the description is returned without them by design.
failureModes.check: Expected on a slow response. Re-running the lookup usually fills dimensions from the cache.

failureModes.symptom: Every lookup is slow again after being fast
failureModes.cause: The learned API template was invalidated by a miss and the app fell back to level 3 page loads.
failureModes.check: One successful level-3 load relearns the template. Persistent slowness means the BO API URL shape changed.

failureModes.symptom: The mode switches to the wrong product family
failureModes.cause: detectModeFromErpDesc classified the description differently, or vehicleType upgraded air to car.
failureModes.check: Set the mode manually. Batch mode is never auto-left.

flows.label: Fill via the operator's real Chrome
flows.summary: The same phase-1 script, executed in the operator's own browser over CDP. Exists because their real profile is already logged in everywhere.

steps.label: Renderer requests the Chrome path
steps.detail: Currently unreferenced from the UI — the button was re-pointed at the API pipeline.

steps.label: Kill Chrome if it is running without the port
steps.detail: A live profile lock makes Chrome silently ignore --remote-debugging-port, so there is no gentler option.

steps.label: Relaunch against the real User Data directory
steps.detail: Polls the port for up to 20 seconds.

steps.label: Find or open the product tab
Connect over a hand-rolled WebSocket
steps.detail: The URL is rewritten from localhost to 127.0.0.1: Windows resolves localhost to ::1, but Chrome listens only on IPv4.

steps.label: Same script, evaluated with awaitPromise
steps.detail: Five-minute timeout. There is no phase 2 on this path — articles are not filled.

failureModes.symptom: 'Chrome is already running without remote debugging'
failureModes.cause: launchChromeForBo refuses to kill Chrome; only fillBoInChrome does that.
failureModes.check: Close Chrome completely, including background tasks, then retry.

failureModes.symptom: CDP call timeout on every command
failureModes.cause: The WebSocket URL resolved to IPv6 ::1 while Chrome listens only on IPv4.
failureModes.check: The localhost to 127.0.0.1 rewrite must stay. Removing it breaks CDP on Windows entirely.

failureModes.symptom: Fill works but articles are never written
failureModes.cause: This transport has no phase 2 by design.
failureModes.check: Use the Electron window path or the API pipeline when articles are needed.

failureModes.symptom: Chrome reopens with a fresh, logged-out profile
failureModes.cause: The --user-data-dir argument did not resolve to the operator's real profile.
failureModes.check: Confirm %LOCALAPPDATA%/Google/Chrome/User Data exists. The whole point of this path is the existing login.

flows.label: Photo upload — fast API path
flows.summary: Skips opening the product in IMG Tool entirely. Faster, but that also means the already-has-photos guard cannot apply — so the identity guards before it carry all the weight.

steps.label: Operator starts the upload queue
steps.detail: The queue is pausable and resumable; a login failure halts it while preserving the position.

steps.label: BO product page opened to read the UID
Two identity guards before anything is written
steps.detail: The loaded URL must still contain the code, and the page text plus every input value must contain it too. Both were added after a live product was overwritten.

steps.label: Product UID read from the GUID-shaped input
Each image posted twice
steps.detail: A multipart upload, then a JSON record carrying uid, colour and eight output sizes. Colour encodes whether it is a base main, a base alt, or a series variation.

steps.label: Series variations get a main image each
steps.detail: The dimension list comes from the correlator, keyed by Dim1.

steps.label: Variation alts assigned by reference
steps.detail: Existing CDN URLs are referenced rather than re-uploaded — re-uploading would duplicate them into the general pool.

failureModes.symptom: abort-url-mismatch or abort-page-mismatch in the log
failureModes.cause: The loaded BO page no longer matched the requested code, so the upload refused to continue.
failureModes.check: This guard is working as intended. Re-run the single code and watch which product actually loads.

failureModes.symptom: Photos overwrote a product that already had them
failureModes.cause: The fast path never opens the product in IMG Tool, so the already-has-photos guard cannot run.
failureModes.check: Use the normal (non-fast) upload when overwriting is a risk. Fast is for known-empty products.

failureModes.symptom: Variation photos duplicated into the general pool
failureModes.cause: Variation alts were re-uploaded through the resize endpoint instead of referenced by existing CDN URL.
failureModes.check: Variation alts must be assigned by reference with colour set to Dim1.

failureModes.symptom: Queue stops partway with needsLogin
failureModes.cause: The IMG Tool or BO session expired mid-run.
failureModes.check: Log in, then press Continue — the queue position was preserved, so completed products are not redone.

flows.label: Scrape → process → upload photos
flows.summary: Finding product photos on supplier sites, squaring and cleaning them locally, then pushing them into IMG Tool. The match logic is deliberately strict.

steps.label: Operator picks a source and pastes code pairs
steps.detail: BO code and supplier code per line, with a jittered 3–7 second throttle between products.

steps.label: A window opens without stealing focus
steps.detail: showInactive, so the operator can still solve a Cloudflare challenge by hand.

steps.label: Confident match, or nothing
steps.detail: Codes under four alphanumerics are rejected, and the slug must contain a delimited in-order token match. It never falls back to the first link.

steps.label: Images downloaded with the source's own Referer
steps.detail: AutoDoc images are upscaled by probing the CDN size parameter and measuring naturalWidth in-page.

steps.label: Squared and cleaned locally
steps.detail: pica resample to a 1000px canvas with a 900px content box, flood-fill background to white, JPEG at quality 0.95.

steps.label: Uploaded, then verified and repaired
steps.detail: A separate read-only verify pass counts mains and alts, and the fix pass re-uploads only the shortfall.

failureModes.symptom: status 'rejected' and no images for a code
failureModes.cause: The supplier slug did not clear the confident-match test, or the code was under four alphanumerics.
failureModes.check: Intentional. Find the product manually and use the single-code lookup or drag the photos in.

failureModes.symptom: Every product returns nothing, suddenly
failureModes.cause: A Cloudflare challenge is blocking the scrape window.
failureModes.check: The window is visible but never focused — bring it up and solve the challenge, then resume.

failureModes.symptom: AutoDoc images are low resolution
failureModes.cause: The upscale probe fell back to the thumbnail because no larger variant measured bigger.
failureModes.check: Expected for some products. Verify against the source page before assuming a bug.

failureModes.symptom: status 'manual_check'
failureModes.cause: Images were found and saved, but the main image did not meet the expected pixel size.
failureModes.check: Open the code in the importer, inspect the frames, and fix or re-fetch from another source.

flows.label: Batch CMS run
flows.summary: The high-volume path: many products from one Excel or AI-generated JSON, run in sequence with live progress and a resumable saved record.

steps.label: Switch to batch mode
steps.detail: The mode sets a data attribute on body; CSS does the rest. The title field and mode toggle physically relocate.

steps.label: Rows entered, imported, or pasted as JSON
steps.detail: Excel parsing is hand-rolled — zip reading, inflate via DecompressionStream, XML parse. No library.

steps.label: Validated and seeded into a saved run
steps.detail: The batch dashboard record lives in IndexedDB; only a light index sits in localStorage.

steps.label: Reviewed product by product in the CMS tab
steps.detail: A navigator replaces the normal copy-card grids in batch mode.

steps.label: Run all, via API or via injection
Each product filled in turn
steps.detail: _isBatch suppresses the title-mismatch guard, since batch titles are supplied rather than derived.

steps.label: Every step reported into the dashboard
steps.detail: dashMark() is the universal report-in hook — CMS, CSE, images and bind all funnel through it.

steps.label: Verified, then repaired
steps.detail: The fix pass re-fills and re-verifies in place, moving products between the issue and clean lists live.

steps.label: Resumable from History
steps.detail: Loading a saved run and resuming skips products whose CMS is already marked done.

failureModes.symptom: A wrong product got filled during a batch
failureModes.cause: _isBatch suppresses the title-word guard, because batch titles are supplied rather than derived from the page.
failureModes.check: The bo_code column is the only identity check in batch mode. Validate the sheet before running, not after.

failureModes.symptom: Run stops early with no error
failureModes.cause: The stop flag was set, or a product returned needsLogin which halts the loop.
failureModes.check: Check the results log for the last code, log in, then resume from History — completed products are skipped.

failureModes.symptom: Excel import produces zero products
failureModes.cause: The sheet matched neither the tall nor the wide layout.
failureModes.check: Download the template and compare headers. The parser is hand-rolled and header-driven.

failureModes.symptom: Progress looks stalled on one code
failureModes.cause: A single fill is waiting on a network floor or a 45s page-load timeout.
failureModes.check: Expected for slow products. The live ETA accounts for it; only intervene if it exceeds the timeout.

flows.label: EDIT tab batch tools
flows.summary: Six one-off tools that write across many products. The FAQ writer is the most dangerous, because a category extras write replaces the whole record.

steps.label: Operator pastes a spec or FAQ array
steps.detail: Clone Articles takes {from, to, names[]}; Category FAQ takes [{iso, question, answer}].

steps.label: A pure module parses and guards it
steps.detail: parseCloneSpec refuses a spec where from equals to, because that would overwrite the source.

steps.label: Preview first — dry run writes nothing
steps.detail: Both tools have a preview mode that reports what would change, including whether the target already exists.

steps.label: The same pure module is required in main
steps.detail: One module, three consumers: renderer, main process and the test suite. That is why its guards cannot drift.

steps.label: One navigation, then in-page fetches
steps.detail: Navigate once to establish the session origin, then loop over every code without renavigating.

steps.label: Optimistic-concurrency guard on FAQ write
steps.detail: The write is refused if the FAQ count or the EN question of the target slot has drifted since it was loaded.

steps.label: Rows posted, then read back and diffed
steps.detail: After writing, the whole extras record is re-read and compared so collateral damage to other slots is visible.

failureModes.symptom: 'that would overwrite the source' on a clone
failureModes.cause: The from and to prefixes are identical.
failureModes.check: Working as intended. Give the clone a distinct target prefix.

failureModes.symptom: FAQ write refused with a count or question mismatch
failureModes.cause: The category's extras record changed between Load and Write.
failureModes.check: Press Load again to refresh the slots, then re-apply. Never bypass this guard — the write replaces the entire record.

failureModes.symptom: Other FAQ slots changed after a write
failureModes.cause: The whole extras record is replaced on write, so a stale in-memory copy silently reverts siblings.
failureModes.check: Read the post-write diff in the log. It exists precisely to surface this.

failureModes.symptom: 'TARGET EXISTS' and nothing is written
failureModes.cause: The destination article already exists and overwrite was not set in the spec.
failureModes.check: Confirm you mean to replace it, then add overwrite to the spec.

flows.label: Verify and fix
flows.summary: Reads live BO values back and compares them to what should be there. Independent of the fill path by design, so a bug can only misreport, never overwrite.

steps.label: bo-verify.js injected in an async wrapper
steps.detail: The async wrapper is load-bearing: a plain one serialised the unresolved Promise to an empty object and made every check falsely pass.

steps.label: Values clicked, read, and escaped
steps.detail: Same traversal as the fill, but Escape instead of Tab, so nothing is committed.

steps.label: Identity cross-checked from BASIC INFO
steps.detail: Reads the Part No. independently of the URL.

steps.label: Fix pass re-fills only what failed

failureModes.symptom: Everything passes, including things you know are wrong
failureModes.cause: The injected verify script resolved to an empty object because its wrapper was not async.
failureModes.check: The classic failure here. The wrapper must be async and must await the inner Promise.

failureModes.symptom: Verify reports issues that are actually correct
failureModes.cause: Expected values came from the payload, not the page, so formatting differences read as mismatches.
failureModes.check: Compare against the live page before running a fix pass. Verify can misreport but never writes.

failureModes.symptom: Report window is empty or stale
failureModes.cause: verify-report.html is overwritten each run and verify-debug.log is truncatable.
failureModes.check: Re-run the verify. Neither artefact is a durable ledger.

flows.label: BO Auditor — read-only SQL
flows.summary: The newest subsystem and the only one that touches the database. Read-only by construction, and the renderer never sees SQL or credentials.

steps.label: Connection probed
steps.detail: A trivial SELECT 1, so a misconfiguration surfaces before a long run.

steps.label: Run requested with checks and brand filter
steps.detail: A re-entrancy guard prevents two concurrent audits.

steps.label: Two SELECTs, joined in JavaScript
steps.detail: Joined in JS rather than SQL to dodge a Greek/Latin1 collation conflict between the two tables.

steps.label: Read-only enforced in code, not just by intent
steps.detail: readOnlyIntent on the connection, and assertReadOnly rejects anything that is not a single SELECT or WITH, including stacked statements.

steps.label: Brand derived per product, then check A1 runs
steps.detail: A1 is part-number and title integrity — corruption, neighbour-copy, foreign part numbers. A2 through A7 are placeholders.

steps.label: Findings filtered, sorted, exported
steps.detail: The table caps at 2,000 DOM rows; CSV export carries the full set.

failureModes.symptom: Probe fails with a connection error
failureModes.cause: MSSQL_* environment variables are missing or the .env file was not loaded.
failureModes.check: Credentials come only from process.env in the main process. The renderer never has them.

failureModes.symptom: A query is rejected before it runs
failureModes.cause: assertReadOnly refused it — not a single SELECT or WITH, or it contained stacked statements.
failureModes.check: Working as intended. This layer is read-only by construction and must stay that way.

failureModes.symptom: Results look truncated
failureModes.cause: The table renders at most 2,000 DOM rows.
failureModes.check: Export the CSV — it carries every finding.

failureModes.symptom: Only check A1 is available
failureModes.cause: A2 through A7 are disabled placeholders in the UI.
failureModes.check: Expected. The auditor is a scaffold with one implemented check.
